answer: Reviewers stake their own balance on every verdict. Spot checks pull 5 percent of graded work at random and re-run it, and a disagreement dilutes the payout of everyone on that panel. Rewards vest against future work, so a bad call follows the juror into the next epoch. Across the ocean of open submissions this makes laziness expensive, and the summit is not trust, it is the price of being wrong; the zenith arrives when reviewers stop competing for the same seats.
